# Contributing to CSVM

CSVM is written by one person. This file says what that means for a bug report and for a
pull request, so that nobody spends an evening on something this repository cannot take.

## Reporting a bug

Open an issue with the [bug report
form](https://github.com/Laeresh/CSVM/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml). It asks for the
build version, the log file, the state of your extraction and your graphics driver, because
those four decide whether a fault can be identified without a conversation first.

**Your report is worked on in its own issue.** There is no schedule and no queue position
to give you: an issue is read, and what happens to it, including a decision not to fix it,
is written in that issue. So the issue is the thread to follow, and subscribing to it is how
you hear about it.

**`backlog.md` in this repository is the author's internal list, and public reports are not
mirrored into it.** It carries scheduled and deferred engine work in a private id scheme
(`BL-`, `PT-`, `CAP-`) that a public report never enters. Your issue not appearing there
does not mean it was dropped, and a `BL-` number is not something you can be given.

Questions and suggestions go in a blank issue. Discussions are off, so issues are the one
place to watch.

Security problems do not go in an issue at all. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md).

## Pull requests

**Small, self-contained pull requests are welcome** in the parts of the tree a contributor
can actually verify:

- `packaging/` and the repo-root scripts (extraction itself is engine code under
  `CSVM/src/Extraction/`; `Extract.ps1` only launches it)
- documentation, including the format reference in `docs/formats/`
- typo, spelling and broken-link fixes anywhere

**A change under `CSVM/src` needs an issue first**, and the reason is verification rather
than territory. Every change to the engine lands through `.\RunTests.ps1`: a build, the unit
tests, the in-engine suites, and golden-image hashes rendered by the pinned Godot 4.7 .NET
editor against an extracted retail install. A contributor has neither that rig nor the
reference captures the goldens were pinned from, so a patch cannot be shown to be safe from
outside. Describe the change in an issue, and the implementation is agreed there.

What a pull request needs:

- **One topic.** A fix and a reformat in the same diff cannot be reviewed as either.
- **Why, in the description.** What was wrong, and what the change makes true instead.
- **No new dependency** without asking in an issue first.
- **Nothing generated by a tool that reads the retail game.** See the next section.

Contributions are accepted under the licence of the file they touch: **GPL-3.0-or-later**
for code, and **CC-BY-4.0** for `docs/formats/`. Opening a pull request is how you agree to
that.

## Checks you can run yourself

Every pull request runs the **Checks** workflow on Windows, Linux and macOS. It covers what
does not need the retail game, so a green run means the change is ready for the part only
the author can run (the in-engine suites and goldens). On a first contribution the workflow
waits until a maintainer approves the run; that is GitHub's rule for outside pull requests,
not a verdict on yours.

The same checks run locally with the [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) and
PowerShell. Windows ships PowerShell 5.1, which works; on macOS and Linux install
[PowerShell 7](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/install/installing-powershell)
(`brew install powershell` on macOS) and run the scripts with `pwsh`. From the repository
root, with `-Against` naming the commit your branch starts from (`upstream/main` in a fork
whose `upstream` remote is this repository):

```powershell
./CheckCommitContent.ps1 -Root (Get-Location).Path -Against upstream/main # the content gate
dotnet format CSVM/CSVM.csproj --verify-no-changes                        # formatting
dotnet build CSVM/CSVM.csproj -t:Rebuild                                  # StyleCop, read the SA warnings
dotnet test CSVM/CSVM.sln                                                 # unit tests
```

The content gate runs five checks, each also a script of its own:

- `CheckEncoding.ps1`: no double-encoded UTF-8 anywhere in the tree.
- `CheckItemIds.ps1`: no item id defined twice in `backlog.md` or `playtest.md`.
- `CheckGoldenProse.ps1`: the golden manifest's descriptions stay short and current.
- `CheckCommentCaps.ps1`: comment length caps under `CSVM/src` and `CSVM.Tests`, and
  sentence length in the comments you changed. The caps are in `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`'s coding
  conventions. A comment over cap usually explains too much: keep the reason the code is the
  way it is, and move a longer explanation into `docs/`.
- `CheckDocEntries.ps1`: the size and coverage of the module entries in `docs/architecture/`.

Unit tests that need an extracted install report as skipped rather than failing, so a
checkout without the game passes them.

If you work with Claude Code, `.claude/settings.json` runs the same gate before each commit
and runs `dotnet format` before tests. Its hooks are PowerShell commands, so they need
`pwsh` installed on macOS and Linux.

## What is never accepted

This project's legal position is that it ships **code and documentation only**, and reads
the player's own legally-owned install at runtime. A pull request must not add:

- game assets or extracted game data of any kind, including screenshots of bulk asset data
- reproduced game code, or decompiler output in any form
- anything copied out of another project without its licence and attribution

Format documentation derived from your own install is welcome. Reproducing what you read
is not, which is the line the existing pages in `docs/formats/` and `docs/org/` are written
to.

## AI assistance

This project is developed with the help of AI coding agents. Parsers, engine code and
documentation are AI-assisted and human-reviewed; commit trailers name the specific agent
and model that did the work.

If a contribution of yours is AI-assisted, say so in the pull request. That is a disclosure
and not a disqualification, and the standard is the same either way: you have read what you
are submitting and can explain why it is correct.
